headline: Google employees question Gemini 4’s real-world performance despite strong benchmarks
summary: Google is facing internal debate regarding whether its Gemini 4 Argon AI model performs as well in real-world coding tasks as its strong benchmark scores suggest. While some employees report inconsistencies in practical usability, others and company leadership maintain that the model operates at the frontier of AI development. The disagreement highlights a broader industry conversation over how effectively standardized testing measures real-world AI performance.

headline: Zypp Electric grants Rs 11 crore in ESOPs to over 250 employees
summary: EV logistics company Zypp Electric has granted Rs 11 crore in ESOPs to over 250 employees across corporate and field roles as it prepares for potential IPO readiness. The grant comes alongside strong financial performance, including an 88% year-on-year revenue increase in Q1, as the firm aims to expand its electric fleet to 100,000 vehicles across 20 cities by FY28.

headline: Saudi employees limited to five contracts a year for Nitaqat counting
summary: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Human Resources has updated its Nitaqat Saudization counting rules on the Qiwa platform to introduce stricter contract limits. To qualify toward a company's quota, Saudi employees must earn at least SR4,000 monthly and have held no more than five employment contracts in the preceding 52 weeks. Additionally, workers are now restricted to holding a maximum of two concurrent jobs and signing no more than seven new contracts per year.

headline: Canada tightens rules on foreign worker sponsorship
summary: Canada has updated its Temporary Foreign Worker Programme to require that only the entity directly managing an employee can apply for Labour Market Impact Assessments (LMIAs). This policy change effectively bans staffing agencies and Employers of Record (EORs) from sponsoring foreign workers on behalf of third-party client businesses. Consequently, Canadian companies must directly sponsor their foreign hires and immediately review existing hiring arrangements to ensure compliance.

headline: From HR operations to COO: Gautami Vinayan joins Utsav Group of Companies
summary: Gautami Vinayan has been appointed as the Chief Operating Officer and HR at Utsav Group of Companies, bridging her background in human resources and operational management. Her career includes previous HR roles at prominent organizations such as Bennett Coleman & Co., Sodexo, and Compass Group. In her new executive position, she will oversee workforce strategy and business operations across the conglomerate's diversified portfolio.

headline: Case-in-Point: The employee who doesn’t want to become a manager
summary: Meridian Software faces a talent management dilemma after one of its top technical contributors repeatedly turned down promotions into management, preferring to focus on engineering problem-solving. HR must now decide whether to continue pushing her toward people leadership, establish a dedicated specialist track, or find an alternative leadership model without direct reports. The case highlights the organizational challenge of offering meaningful career progression for high performers who prefer individual contribution over management.

headline: Mahesh Muralidhar Pai to take charge as MD & CEO, South Indian Bank
summary: South Indian Bank has appointed Mahesh Muralidhar Pai as its Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, effective October 1, 2026. Pai brings nearly three decades of experience from Canara Bank, where he recently served as Chief General Manager leading digital transformation and overseas operations. In his new role, he aims to focus on driving sustainable business growth, advancing digital capabilities, and strengthening customer relationships.

headline: Is Apple’s new CEO planning workforce cuts?
summary: Apple's new chief executive, John Ternus, is reportedly planning targeted, small-scale layoffs and project cancellations to streamline operations. The decision stems from mounting financial pressures, including surging costs from a global memory chip shortage and declining quarterly services revenue. The workforce reductions aim to protect profitability while reallocating resources toward core, high-growth areas.

headline: JPMorgan names Mark O’Donovan as new HR head
summary: JPMorgan Chase has appointed Mark O’Donovan as its next head of human resources, effective January 2027, succeeding retiring HR leader Robin Leopold. O’Donovan, currently CEO of international consumer banking, brings three decades of financial and operational leadership to the position. The succession reflects a growing trend in global finance to integrate people strategy directly with technology and core business operations.

headline: herSTORY: Sonal Jain, Global Chief HR & Transformation Officer, EPL
summary: Sonal Jain, Global Chief HR & Transformation Officer at EPL, reflects on her leadership evolution, emphasizing a shift from seeking approval to driving fairness and value creation. She highlights abundance, courage, and clear governance as key to leading teams through organizational change effectively. Furthermore, Jain stresses that future readiness requires building continuous learning agility and talent capabilities alongside technological adoption.

headline: HCLTech offers Rs 18 lakh starting salary as it steps up ‘Elite Engineer’ hiring
summary: HCLTech is adopting a skills-based fresher hiring strategy for its FY27 intake of roughly 11,000 graduates, widening its starting salary range from Rs 4.5 lakh up to Rs 18 lakh. The top-tier 'Elite Engineer' cadre targets candidates skilled in high-demand areas like AI, semiconductors, and quantum computing. This widening pay scale reflects a broader trend where specific high-value technical skills dictate entry-level compensation over traditional engineering degrees.

headline: Former Ford employee alleges forced-ranking system used to drive ‘soft layoffs’
summary: A former Ford employee has filed a lawsuit alleging that the automaker used a forced-ranking performance system to execute covert workforce reductions. The complaint claims that management enforced mandatory low performance quotas to dismiss older workers approaching retirement milestones without conducting formal layoffs. The lawsuit includes claims under age discrimination, disability discrimination, and retirement security laws.

headline: DoorDash opens first India office in Hyderabad, plans to scale workforce to 3,000
summary: DoorDash has launched its first India-based facility in Hyderabad, starting operations with 500 employees and aiming to scale to over 3,000 workers within two years. The center will focus on customer experience, integrity, and administration to support the company's global platform and monthly active user base. The move highlights Hyderabad's rising status as a key global capability hub for international tech companies.

headline: adfest gets a new logo designed by Santosh Padhi and Into Creative
summary: AdFest has unveiled a minimalist new logo designed by Into Creative's Santosh Padhi ahead of the advertising festival's 30th anniversary. Inspired by a bent strip of paper and a lotus, the updated identity reflects the event's heritage while looking toward the future of creative industries. The milestone event will take place from March 18 to 20, 2027, in Pattaya, Thailand.

headline: Parachute Advansed Jasmine shines a light on confidence
summary: Marico has launched a new campaign for its Parachute Advansed Jasmine Coconut Hair Oil, targeting young women across television and digital platforms in India. Conceptualized by Team WPP, the advertisement connects deep hair nourishment and healthy shine with self-expression and personal confidence. The initiative seeks to align the personal care brand with contemporary beauty routines during key life moments.

headline: Sony LIV’s Asian Games 2026 coverage sets new revenue record
summary: Sony LIV’s coverage of the 2026 Asian Games has achieved record advertising revenue, making it the platform's highest-grossing multi-sport event to date. Driven by broad multi-sport viewer engagement and key moments like India's cricket campaign, over 18 major brands have secured sponsorship packages. The milestone underscores the expanding commercial appeal and digital audience reach of multi-sport broadcasts in India.

headline: Traya puts women’s hair fall on display in Mumbai activation
summary: Traya Health launched an experiential marketing activation at Mumbai's Bandra Bandstand featuring a seven-foot visual installation to raise awareness about female hair loss and thinning. The event offered visitors complimentary scalp scans and hair coaching consultations to promote the brand's personalized, holistic treatment solutions. The initiative aimed to educate women on the internal root causes of hair fall, such as hormonal shifts, nutritional gaps, and stress.
